text: Lay awake wondering if this whole idea is worth the months. A journal that remembers what you wrote sounds lovely when I say it out loud, but maybe it's only lovely to me. Plenty of note apps exist already. What if I'm building something nobody asked for, and the only reason it feels important is that I'm the one making it?

Read a little Marcus Aurelius on the bus. He keeps coming back to the idea that the only thing truly ours is how we respond, not what happens to us. I like that, but I'm not sure I believe it fully. If I can't control the outcome of my work, why does it still feel like the outcome is what makes it count?

Walked to the lake before breakfast. The water was completely still and two herons stood in the shallows like they had nowhere to be. I bought a warm croissant on the way back and ate it on the bench. Nothing happened and it was one of the best mornings in weeks.

It works! The app finally linked tonight's entry to something I wrote in August, without me tagging anything. I actually laughed out loud at my desk. Months of plumbing and suddenly it does the one thing I wanted it to do. I can't wait to show someone.

Big companies have teams of thirty people building things like this. I'm one person with evenings and weekends. The idea might be fine, but can I really execute it well enough alone? Every bug I fix seems to reveal two more, and I'm not sure I have the skill to finish it properly.

If I rewrite every sentence of an old entry, is it still my thought? I keep thinking about the ship of Theseus. Maybe a self works the same way: every plank replaced, and still somehow the same boat. A journal might be the only place where you can see the planks being swapped.

Dinner at Maya's. Six of us around a table too small, someone burned the rice, and nobody cared. We laughed until my cheeks hurt over a story about her cat and the Christmas tree. I walked home feeling full in every sense.

Showed the demo to Sam over coffee. He wrote a line about missing his dad, and the app quietly surfaced a note he'd written weeks earlier about the same thing. He went silent for a second and then said, 'oh, that's the thing.' I've been buzzing all afternoon.

Opened my old notes from when I started this project and felt embarrassed by how confident I sounded. Now I doubt half of the ideas. Maybe the reflections are too gentle to be useful, maybe the memory feature is a gimmick. I don't know if I'm refining the idea or just losing faith in it.

What does it mean to pay attention? Simone Weil said attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity. Writing every day feels like a way of paying attention to my own life, which sounds selfish, but maybe it's the opposite. You can't give attention to others if you've never practised it on yourself.

Rain all afternoon, so I made ginger tea and read by the window with the radiator ticking. Mum called and we talked for an hour about nothing in particular: her tomatoes, my cousin's wedding, the neighbour's new dog. I felt properly at home.

Built the first installer today and ran it on a clean laptop. It opened, downloaded the models by itself, and wrote my first reflection. Seeing it work on a machine that isn't mine made it feel real for the first time. Release is close. I keep grinning at the screen.

Scope keeps growing: letters, patterns, fonts, a writing dial. Every addition feels right on its own, but together I worry it's turning into a pile of half-finished features. Am I executing a clear idea, or hiding from shipping by adding one more thing?

Back to the Stoics. Epictetus says some things are up to us and some are not. My effort is up to me; whether people like the app is not. When I hold that clearly, the anxiety goes quiet. When I forget it, I start measuring myself by numbers I've never even seen.

Saturday hike with the twins. We got lost twice, found a waterfall nobody had told us about, and ate squashed sandwiches on a warm rock. My legs are wrecked and I'm completely happy. I want more days that feel this simple.

Tagged the release candidate. Wrote the README tonight and for once the words came easily, because I know exactly what this thing is for. A journal that helps you notice when you're thinking a thought again. I'm so excited to put it out into the world.

A week before release and the doubt is back, louder. What if people try it once and never open it again? What if the reflections feel generic, or the install breaks on their machine? I keep reading my own feature list and wondering whether any of it is good enough to share.

I keep circling the same question: am I the person who wrote my first entry, or someone new who just inherited the notes? Maybe identity is less a thing and more a thread, and remembering is how we keep pulling it through. That might be why this project matters to me.

Sunny morning, open window, a good playlist and nothing urgent. I made pancakes for no reason and ate them on the balcony. Called Maya just to say hi. Small, ordinary happiness, and I noticed it while it was happening, which feels new.

Tomorrow it goes public. I've packed the installer, written the release notes, and checked everything twice. Nervous, yes, but mostly I feel lit up. Something I made, start to finish, is about to be in other people's hands. Whatever happens, I built it and I'm shipping it.
